_comment: Per-machine config. config.json is gitignored; copy this file to config.json and adjust paths. The box (guppy) keeps its own config.json with local paths.

llm._comment: Small self-assessment model (assess/elicitation/fidelity review). Runs on THIS machine's local ollama; bootstrap sets base_url from --llm-url (default http://127.0.0.1:11434) and pulls `model` if it is missing. This is deliberately local — only codegen travels to a remote host.

codegen._comment: OpenAI-compatible model that writes runnable skill bodies. Runs on a REMOTE ollama host (bootstrap sets base_url from --codegen-url, default guppy http://192.168.8.181:11434); the local small model is `llm` above. Bodies perform real actions against the user's configured services via stdlib transports, read every operational value from ctx.config, and declare their integration (INTEGRATION: service/transport/config_vars). Larger/slower than the decision or self-assessment model. The transport always streams so the client-side token budget (output cap / peak total fill) can abort a runaway in real time; stream only toggles console echo of tokens. timeout is total seconds; idle_warn/idle_timeout surface a silent (wedged) stream. The context window is auto-detected via ollama /api/show; context_window is the manual fallback (0 = auto/default 100000). smart_limit/warn_limit and max_fill_ratio/warn_fill_ratio bound total fill; max_output caps streamed output (>=1 absolute tokens, 0<x<1 fraction of window); chars_per_token converts chars to the token estimate. temperature/top_p/presence_penalty/frequency_penalty follow the Qwen3.8 model card's instruct-mode anti-repetition guidance (high presence_penalty, not greedy temperature); generate_skill_body escalates to presence 2.0 / temp 0.5 on retries (max_attempts attempts, fresh short prompt each time). elicitation asks the product owner implementation questions before the body is written (REPL inline; dashboard deferred). After the body lands it is reviewed for real-action fidelity, then the data contract (contract.json) is derived in a separate call, then skill.test.py (hermetic mechanics test: loopback http.server for HTTP bodies, fixtures inline, no external network) in a shared-context call, and the test is auto-run as a subprocess (test_timeout seconds); on failure a 3-option SemIf decision (code/contract/test) regenerates the failing piece, bounded by test_max_attempts. contract_search.enabled auto-populates the skill config.json via SemIf against the global + category config.

elicitation._comment: Ask the product owner implementation questions before the body is written: which service/account, how to connect, where the credential comes from, what success looks like. The REPL wires an inline asker; the dashboard defers questions to the questions panel and the single-slot writer waits up to wait_timeout seconds. Questions never ask for operational data values (collected at first fire) or config-vs-input cadence (the config step owns that).

fidelity._comment: After the body lands, the small self-assessment model reviews whether it really performs the action vs simulates it (canned result, fabricated data, draft-by-default). Static INTEGRATION checks (declaration vs code) run alongside. A rejected body is regenerated with the finding, bounded by max_attempts; a still-fake body is accepted but traced/badged, never a hard authoring failure. A missing reviewer degrades to accept.

repair._comment: A failed real run triggers a logged SemIf repair choice (retry / repair_skill / ask_user / no_repair) surfaced in the REPL and dashboard. Executing a repair is user-confirmed (a codegen write is slow); body repairs are bounded by max_attempts per skill and carry the observed failure into the regeneration.

contract_search._comment: After the data contract lands, run a SemIf choice per variable to auto-populate the skill config.json from the global config and the category config (data/skills/<category>/config.json). Logged as phase config:search.

degeneration._comment: SemIf degeneration watchdog: while the body streams, a 2-option SemIf decision (continue/stop) is made every `interval` chars against the last `window` chars of content+reasoning (once `min_chars` have accumulated); P(stop) >= threshold aborts the write with a graceful stub. Recorded trace-only (kind `codegen`), never in the decision log. Disabled when no engine is available.

simplex_chat._comment: Pinned simplex-chat daemon that the messenger gateway talks to. bootstrap.sh downloads this exact binary (sha256 verified) into .runtime/bin/, runs it headless on `port` with its profile in .runtime/simplex/, and renders the semif-simplex.service unit from it. Bump version/bin_url/sha256 together. The gateway's ws_url (gateway.simplex.ws_url) must match `port`.

gateway._comment: Messenger intake. `python -m semif_agent.cli gateway` connects to the local simplex-chat daemon (see `simplex_chat` above) over its JSON WebSocket API and feeds authorized DM text through the normal gate/score/queue/dispatch pipeline; results, authoring questions, and repair offers are sent back to the originating chat. Requires the optional `websockets` package (lazy-imported; the gateway refuses to start without it). allowed_users entries match either a numeric contactId or a display name; default is deny-all unless allow_all_users is set. home_channel receives messages whose origin chat is unknown (e.g. a background repair offer). text_batch_delay concatenates rapid-fire messages from one contact. `user_id` is the daemon user whose contact address the connect-link lookup shows/creates (default 1). Groups/attachments are not supported in this first cut.

inbox._comment: Buffer every authorized inbound DM so a read skill can pull it (see `messaging_bridge_url`). dispatch=true keeps the current behavior (also submit the message as a scheduler request); set dispatch=false for pull-only mode, where inbound messages are buffered and only acted on when the user asks.

bridge._comment: Local HTTP API the gateway serves to skills (send/read SimpleX messages). Skills call it over `http` with the top-level `messaging_bridge_url`; keep that URL in sync with host/port. GET /address shows/creates the bot's contact link (wired to the adapter); /health, /contacts, /inbox, /inbox/next and POST /send are the rest. Binds localhost only; an optional `token` is required in the X-Semif-Token header when set. Set enabled=false to run the gateway without the bridge.
